title: Arakhin 7
description: Whether a condemned man’s damages are collected from his heirs, whether his offerings are brought before his execution, the pregnant woman taken to be executed and the woman who dies in childbirth, the hair of an executed woman, and, opening the second chapter, the least and the most a valuation can cost.
topics: 💰 A loan by oral agreement and a loan written in the Torah: Rav Yosef and Rabba on collecting from heirs
🕳️ The pit, the ox and the digger: judges sitting at the opening of the pit
🐑 One taken to be executed: his sin offering’s blood is sprinkled, but a new sin does not delay him
🤰 A pregnant woman taken to be executed, and one already on the travailing chair
🔪 A woman who died in labor on Shabbat: bringing a knife through the public domain to save the child
💇 Her hair, her wig and the verdict: Rav, Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak and Levi’s baraitot
📖 Hadran: the first chapter, HaKol Ma’arikhin, ends
⚖️ Chapter 2 opens: no valuation below a sela or above fifty, and Rav Adda bar Ahava’s two vows

a1.he: מִכְּלָל דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: נִיתַּן לַחֲזָרַת עֲמִידַת בֵּית דִּין?!

a2.he: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: בְּמִלְוָה עַל פֶּה גּוֹבֶה מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁין קָמִיפַּלְגִי, תַּנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: מִלְוָה עַל פֶּה גּוֹבֶה מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁין, וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר סָבַר: אֵינוֹ גּוֹבֶה מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁין.

a3.he: רַבָּה אָמַר: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִלְוָה עַל פֶּה אֵינוֹ גּוֹבֶה מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁין, וְהָכָא בְּמִלְוָה הַכְּתוּבָה בַּתּוֹרָה כִּכְתוּבָה בִּשְׁטָר קָמִיפַּלְגִי, תַּנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: כִּכְתוּבָה בִּשְׁטָר דָּמְיָא, וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר סָבַר: לָאו כִּכְתוּבָה בִּשְׁטָר דָּמְיָא.

a4.he: מֵיתִיבִי: הַחוֹפֵר בּוֹר בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, וְנָפַל עָלָיו שׁוֹר וַהֲרָגוֹ — פָּטוּר, וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא שֶׁאִם מֵת הַשּׁוֹר — יוֹרְשֵׁי בַּעַל הַבּוֹר חַיָּיבִין לְשַׁלֵּם דְּמֵי שׁוֹר לִבְעָלָיו!

a5.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילָא אָמַר רַב: כְּשֶׁעָמַד בַּדִּין, וְהָא ״הֲרָגוֹ״ קָתָנֵי! אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: כְּשֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ טְרֵיפָה.

a6.he: וְהָאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, תָּנֵי חַגָּא: מֵת וּקְבָרוֹ! וְהִילְכְתָא דְּיָיתְבִי דַּיָּינֵי אַפּוּמָּא דְבֵירָא.

a7.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַיּוֹצֵא לֵיהָרֵג — מַזִּין עָלָיו מִדַּם חַטָּאתוֹ וּמִדַּם אֲשָׁמוֹ, חָטָא בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה — אֵין נִזְקָקִין לוֹ. מַאי טַעְמָא? אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין מְעַנִּין אֶת דִּינוֹ.

a8.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ רֵישָׁא נָמֵי! כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיָה זִבְחוֹ זָבוּחַ בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה.

a9.he: אֲבָל אֵין זִבְחוֹ זָבוּחַ, מַאי? לָא? אַדְּתָנֵי ״חָטָא בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה אֵין נִזְקָקִין לוֹ״, לִיפְלוֹג וְלִיתְנֵי בְּדִידַהּ: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים — שֶׁהָיָה זֶבַח זָבוּחַ בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה, אֲבָל אֵין זֶבַח זָבוּחַ — לֹא!

a10.he: הָכִי נָמֵי קָאָמַר: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים — שֶׁהָיָה זֶבַח זָבוּחַ בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה, אֲבָל אֵין זֶבַח זָבוּחַ — נַעֲשָׂה כְּמִי שֶׁחָטָא בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה, וְאֵין נִזְקָקִין לוֹ.

a11.he: מַתְנִי׳ הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁיָּצְאָה לֵיהָרֵג, אֵין מַמְתִּינִין לָהּ עַד שֶׁתֵּלֵד. הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁיָּשְׁבָה עַל הַמַּשְׁבֵּר, מַמְתִּינִין לָהּ עַד שֶׁתֵּלֵד. הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁנֶּהֶרְגָה, נֶהֱנִין בִּשְׂעָרָהּ. בְּהֵמָה שֶׁנֶּהֶרְגָה, אֲסוּרָה בַּהֲנָאָה.

a12.he: גְּמָ׳ פְּשִׁיטָא, גּוּפַהּ הִיא! אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וּכְתִיב ״כַּאֲשֶׁר יָשִׁית עָלָיו בַּעַל הָאִשָּׁה״, מָמוֹנָא דְבַעַל הוּא, וְלָא לַיפְסְדֵיהּ מִינֵּיהּ, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

a13.he: וְאֵימָא הָכִי נָמֵי! אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אָמַר קְרָא ״וּמֵתוּ גַּם שְׁנֵיהֶם״ — לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַוָּולָד.

a14.he: וְהַאי מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ, עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ שְׁנֵיהֶן שָׁוִין, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה! כִּי קָאָמְרִינַן מִ״גַּם״.

a15.he: יָשְׁבָה עַל הַמַּשְׁבֵּר וְכוּ׳. מַאי טַעְמָא? כֵּיוָן דְּעָקַר, גּוּפָא אַחֲרִינָא הוּא.

a16.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הָאִשָּׁה הַיּוֹצְאָה לֵיהָרֵג, מַכִּין אוֹתָהּ כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית הֵרָיוֹן, כְּדֵי שֶׁיָּמוּת הַוָּולָד תְּחִילָּה, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תָּבֹא לִידֵי נִיוּוּל. לְמֵימְרָא דְּהִיא קָדְמָה וּמֵתָה בְּרֵישָׁא? וְהָא קַיְימָא לַן דְּוָולָד מָיֵית בְּרֵישָׁא!

a17.he: דִּתְנַן: תִּינוֹק בֶּן יוֹמוֹ נוֹחֵל וּמַנְחִיל, וְאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: נוֹחֵל בְּנִכְסֵי הָאֵם לְהַנְחִיל לָאַחִין מִן הָאָב.

a18.he: דַּוְוקָא בֶּן יוֹם אֶחָד, אֲבָל עוּבָּר — לָא, דְּהוּא מָיֵית בְּרֵישָׁא, וְאֵין הַבֵּן יוֹרֵשׁ אֶת אִמּוֹ בְּקֶבֶר לְהַנְחִיל לָאַחִין מִן הָאָב!

a19.he: הָנֵי מִילֵּי לְגַבֵּי מִיתָה, אַיְּידֵי דְּוָולָד זוּטְרָא חַיּוּתֵיהּ, עָיְילָא טִיפָּה דְּמַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת וּמְחַתֵּךְ לְהוּ לְסִימָנִין, אֲבָל נֶהֶרְגָה — הִיא מֵתָה בְּרֵישָׁא.

a20.he: וְהָא הֲוָה עוֹבָדָא, וּפַרְכֵּיס עַד תְּלָת פִּרְכּוּסֵי! מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵי אַזְּנַב הַלְּטָאָה דִּמְפַרְכֶּסֶת.

a21.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁיָּשְׁבָה עַל הַמַּשְׁבֵּר וּמֵתָה בְּשַׁבָּת, מְבִיאִין סַכִּין וּמְקָרְעִים אֶת כְּרֵיסָהּ, וּמוֹצִיאִין אֶת הַוָּולָד. פְּשִׁיטָא, מַאי עָבֵיד?

b1.he: מְחַתֵּךְ בְּבָשָׂר הוּא! אָמַר רַבָּה: לֹא נִצְרְכָה לְהָבִיא סַכִּין דֶּרֶךְ רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים.

b2.he: וּמַאי קָמַשְׁמַע לַן, דְּמִסְּפֵיקָא מְחַלְּלִינַן שַׁבְּתָא? תְּנֵינָא: מִי שֶׁנָּפְלָה עָלָיו מַפּוֹלֶת, סָפֵק הוּא שָׁם, סָפֵק אֵינוֹ שָׁם, סָפֵק חַי, סָפֵק מֵת, סָפֵק נׇכְרִי, סָפֵק יִשְׂרָאֵל — מְפַקְּחִין עָלָיו אֶת הַגַּל!

b3.he: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: הָתָם הוּא דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ חֲזָקָה דְּחַיּוּתָא, אֲבָל הָכָא דְּלָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ חֲזָקָה דְּחַיּוּתָא מֵעִיקָּרָא — אֵימָא לָא, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

b4.he: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁנֶּהֶרְגָה וְכוּ׳. וְאַמַּאי? אִיסּוּרֵי הֲנָאָה נִינְהוּ! אָמַר רַב: בְּאוֹמֶרֶת ״תְּנוּ שְׂעָרִי לְבִתִּי״. אִילּוּ אָמְרָה ״תְּנוּ יָדִי לְבִתִּי״, מִי יָהֲבִינַן לַהּ?!

b5.he: אָמַר רַב: בְּפֵאָה נׇכְרִית, טַעְמָא דְּאָמְרָה ״תְּנוּ״, הָא לֹא אָמְרָה ״תְּנוּ״ — גּוּפַהּ הוּא וּמִיתְּסַר.

b6.he: וְהָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, דְּבָעֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: שְׂעַר נָשִׁים צִדְקָנִיּוֹת מַהוּ?

b7.he: וְאָמַר רָבָא: בְּפֵאָה נׇכְרִית לָא קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ, כִּי קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא דִּתְלֵי בְּסִיכְּתָא.

b8.he: הָכָא דִּמְחַבַּר בַּהּ, טַעְמָא דְּאָמְרָה ״תְּנוּ״, הָא לֹא אָמְרָה ״תְּנוּ״ — גּוּפַהּ הוּא וּמִיתְּסַר.

b9.he: קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ לְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, וְהָא דּוּמְיָא דִּבְהֵמָה קָתָנֵי, מָה הָתָם גּוּפַיהּ — אַף הָכָא נָמֵי גּוּפַיהּ!

b10.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: זוֹ מִיתָתָהּ אוֹסַרְתָּהּ, וְזוֹ גְּמַר דִּינָה אוֹסַרְתָּהּ.

b11.he: תָּנֵי לֵוִי כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַב, תָּנֵי לֵוִי כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק. תָּנֵי לֵוִי כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַב: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁיּוֹצְאָה לֵיהָרֵג וְאָמְרָה: ״תְּנוּ שְׂעָרִי לְבִתִּי״ — נוֹתְנִין, מֵתָה — אֵין נוֹתְנִין, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַמֵּת אָסוּר בַּהֲנָאָה.

b12.he: פְּשִׁיטָא! אֶלָּא שֶׁנּוֹיֵי הַמֵּת אָסוּר בַּהֲנָאָה.

b13.he: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁמֵּתָה — נֶהֱנִין בִּשְׂעָרָהּ, בְּהֵמָה שֶׁנֶּהֶרְגָה — אֲסוּרָה בַּהֲנָאָה; וּמָה הֶפְרֵשׁ בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה? זוֹ — מִיתָתָהּ אוֹסַרְתָּהּ, וְזוֹ — גָּמַר דִּינָה אוֹסַרְתָּהּ.

b15.he: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין נֶעֱרָכִין פָּחוֹת מִסֶּלַע, וְלֹא יָתֵר עַל חֲמִשִּׁים סֶלַע. כֵּיצַד? נָתַן סֶלַע וְהֶעֱשִׁיר — אֵינוֹ נוֹתֵן כְּלוּם, פָּחוֹת מִסֶּלַע וְהֶעֱשִׁיר — נוֹתֵן חֲמִשִּׁים סֶלַע.

b16.he: הָיוּ בְּיָדָיו חָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ נוֹתֵן אֶלָּא אַחַת, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: נוֹתֵן אֶת כּוּלָּן. אֵין נֶעֱרָכִין פָּחוֹת מִסֶּלַע, וְלֹא יָתֵר עַל חֲמִשִּׁים סֶלַע.

b17.he: גּמ׳ אֵין נֶעֱרָכִין פָּחוֹת מִסֶּלַע. מְנָלַן? דִּכְתִיב: ״וְכׇל עֶרְכְּךָ יִהְיֶה בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ״, כׇּל עֲרָכִין שֶׁאַתָּה מַעֲרִיךְ לֹא יְהוּ פְּחוּתִין מִשְׁקָל.

b18.he: וְלֹא יָתֵר עַל חֲמִשִּׁים סְלָעִים. דִּכְתִיב: ״חֲמִשִּׁים״.

b19.he: הָיוּ בְּיָדָיו חֲמִשָּׁה כּוּ׳. מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר? כְּתִיב ״חֲמִשִּׁים״ וּכְתִיב ״שֶׁקֶל״, אוֹ חֲמִשִּׁים אוֹ שֶׁקֶל.

b20.he: וְרַבָּנַן? הַהוּא, לְכׇל עֲרָכִין שֶׁאַתָּה מַעֲרִיךְ לֹא יְהוּ פְּחוּתִים מִשְׁקָל הוּא דַּאֲתָא, הֵיכָא דְּאִית לֵיהּ — אָמַר קְרָא: ״אֲשֶׁר תַּשִּׂיג יַד הַנּוֹדֵר״, וַהֲרֵי יָדוֹ מַשֶּׂגֶת.

b21.he: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר? הָהוּא ״יַד הַנּוֹדֵר וְלֹא יַד הַנִּידָּר״ הוּא דַּאֲתָא, וְרַבָּנַן, לָאו מִמֵּילָא שָׁמְעַתְּ מִינַּהּ דְּהֵיכָא דְּיָדוֹ מַשֶּׂגֶת שְׁקוֹל מִינֵּיהּ?

b22.he: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: הָיוּ בְּיָדָיו חָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים, וְאָמַר ״עֶרְכִּי עָלַי״, וְחָזַר וְאָמַר ״עֶרְכִּי עָלַי״, וְנָתַן אַרְבַּע לַשְּׁנִיָּה וְאֶחָד לָרִאשׁוֹנָה — יָצָא יְדֵי שְׁתֵּיהֶן.

b23.he: מַאי טַעְמָא? בַּעַל חוֹב מְאוּחָר שֶׁקָּדַם וְגָבָה — מַה שֶּׁגָּבָה גָּבָה.

b24.he: בְּעִידָּנָא דְּיָהֵיב לַשְּׁנִיָּה, מְשַׁעְבַּד לְרִאשׁוֹנָה. בְּעִידָּנָא דְּיָהֵיב לָרִאשׁוֹנָה, תּוּ לֵית לֵיהּ.

messages.text: 7a

Continued from 6b: a baraita taught that one taken to be executed who injured another is liable, and Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said that he is exempt even then, since he cannot be brought back to stand before the court.

If so, can one conclude by inference that the first tanna holds that one who is being taken to be executed can be brought back to stand before the court for judgment? This is clearly erroneous, as the court is not permitted to delay his execution.

notes.he: בתמיה:
notes.en: By inference that the first tanna holds, etc.: [this is said] in astonishment.

messages.text: Everyone agrees that his execution may not be delayed. Rather, they disagree as to whether or not one who is owed money from a loan by oral agreement can collect from the heirs.
messages.quote: can be brought back to stand before the court

notes.he: אמר רב יוסף במלוה כו':
notes.en: Rav Yosef said: [they disagree] about a loan, etc.

messages.text: The first tanna holds that one who is owed money from a loan by oral agreement can collect from the heirs, and therefore the injured party can collect from the heirs after the execution. But Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar holds that one who is owed money from a loan by oral agreement cannot collect from the heirs, and therefore the heirs are exempt from payment for the injury.
On 6b the daf gave the second explanation in the name of Rava; here the text reads Rabba.

Actually, everyone agrees that one who is owed money from a loan by oral agreement cannot collect from the heirs; and here the tanna’im disagree with regard to whether a loan that is written in the Torah, e.g., one’s obligation to pay if he causes damage, is considered as though it is written in a document.
messages.quote: a loan by oral agreement

messages.text: The first tanna holds that a loan that is written in the Torah is considered as though it is written in a document, and may be collected from the heirs. And Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar holds that it is not considered as though it is written in a document, and therefore it may not be collected.
The Gemara raises an objection against the opinion that one cannot collect a loan that is written in the Torah from the heirs, from a baraita:

If one was digging a pit in the public thoroughfare, and an ox fell on the digger of the pit and killed him, the owner of the ox is exempt from paying damages, as the digger of the pit should not have dug the pit.

notes.he: השור הרג את החופר:
notes.en: And it killed him: the ox killed the digger.

notes.he: בעל השור:
notes.en: Exempt: the owner of the ox.

notes.he: בעל השור שלא היה לו לחפור ברשות הרבים:
notes.en: And it killed him, exempt: the owner of the ox, since [the digger] should not have dug in the public domain.

messages.text: Moreover, if the ox died as a result of the fall, the heirs of the owner of the pit are liable to pay the value of the ox to its owner.

notes.he: אלמא מלוה הכתובה בתורה ככתובה בשטר דמיא וקשיא למאן דאוקי פלוגתייהו דרבי יוסי ות"ק דמתני' באם הזיק דא"כ קשיא סתמא אסתמא. ואיכא דמותיב הך תיובתא לר"ש בן אלעזר אבל פליאה בעיני היאך יכול להקשות הא ר"ש תנא הוא ופליג:
notes.en: Are liable to pay: evidently a loan written in the Torah is considered like one written in a document. And this is difficult for the one who established the dispute of Rabbi Yosei and the first tanna of the mishna [on 6b] as concerning where he caused damage, since if so, an anonymous ruling contradicts an anonymous ruling. And there are those who raise this objection against Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar; but it is a wonder in my eyes how one can raise it, since Rabbi Shimon is a tanna and may disagree.

notes.he: גם השור יורשי בעל הבור חייבין לשלם וקשיא למ"ד מלוה הכתובה באורייתא לאו ככתובה בשטר דמיא:
notes.en: But if [the ox] died: if the ox died too, the heirs of the owner of the pit are liable to pay. And this is difficult for the one who says that a loan written in the Torah is not like one written in a document.

messages.text: This shows that an obligation that is written in the Torah, such as compensation for damage, is collected from heirs.

notes.he: לרבה פריך דאמר לעיל מצוה הכתובה בתורה לאו ככתובה בשטר דמיא וכן העתיק ר"ת בספרו ומצי נמי למפרך לרב יוסף דהא סבר נמי שיעבודא לאו דאורייתא אלא פירש דבריו יותר:
notes.en: They raised an objection: one who digs a pit in the public domain: this objects to Rabba, who said above that a loan written in the Torah is not like one written in a document; and so Rabbeinu Tam copied it in his book. It could also have objected to Rav Yosef, since he too holds that a lien is not by Torah law; but [it objects to Rabba because] he spelled out his view more explicitly.

messages.text: The baraita is dealing with a case where the digger of the pit stood trial for the damage before he died, and once judgment is rendered by a court the resulting financial obligation is comparable to a written loan, not one that is written in the Torah.
messages.quote: the heirs of the owner of the pit are liable to pay

notes.he: קודם שמת וחייבוהו לשלם לפיכך גובה מן היורשין דכיון דדינו חרוץ לשלם ה"ל כמלוה בשטר:
notes.en: When he stood trial: before he died, and they obligated him to pay. Therefore one collects from the heirs, since once his judgment to pay has been decided, it is like a loan with a document.

notes.dh: אמר רב אילא א"ר כשעמד בדין
notes.he: לאו משום קושיא דרבה משני רב הכי שהרי רבה שנים רבות אחר רב היה אלא משום דפרכינן ליה מיניה בפרק גט פשוט (ב"ב דף קעה:) דאמר התם דמלוה על פה אינו גובה מן היורשין ולנפשיה משני:
notes.en: Rabbi Ila said that Rav said: when he stood trial: Rav did not give this answer because of Rabba’s difficulty, since Rabba lived many years after Rav. Rather, it is because an objection is raised against Rav from this [baraita] in chapter Get Pashut (Bava Batra 175b), where he says that a loan by oral agreement is not collected from the heirs; and he gave the answer for his own view.

notes.he: לעולם לאו ככתובה בשטר דמיא אלא משום הכי חייבין יורשין בשעמד בעל הבור בדין ונתחייב קודם שמת:
notes.en: Rabbi Ila said: actually it is not like one written in a document; but the heirs are liable here because the owner of the pit stood trial and was obligated before he died.

messages.text: But it is taught in the baraita that the ox killed him.
messages.quote: and killed him

notes.he: והא הרגו קתני חייבין דלא הוה ליה שהות למיקם בדין:
notes.en: But it teaches “killed him” and [the heirs] are liable; [so] he had no time to stand trial.

messages.text: The baraita does not mean that the ox literally killed him, rather, that it rendered him as one who has a wound that will cause him to die within twelve months [tereifa], and there was enough time before his death to sentence him to pay damages.
messages.quote: killed him

notes.he: שור לבעל הבור טרפה וקם בדין והדר מית:
notes.en: That it made him: the ox made the owner of the pit a tereifa, and he stood trial and then died.

messages.text: But doesn’t Rav Naḥman say that Ḥagga teaches a slightly different version of the baraita, that if the digger of the pit died from the impact of the ox, and the ox effectively buried him in the ground at the bottom of the pit, his heirs have to pay damages to the owner of the ox? In this scenario, how could it be possible for the digger to stand trial?

notes.he: השור בבור כגון שהפיל עמו חוליא ואפ"ה חייבין יורשין:
notes.en: But doesn’t Ḥagga teach: died and buried him: [i.e., the ox buried him] in the pit, for example, it knocked down a section [of earth] with it; and even so the heirs are liable. [Rashi’s heading reads “But doesn’t Ḥagga teach,” without “Rav Naḥman says.”]

notes.he: שקברו שור בנפילתו לבעל הבור שהפיל עליו אדמה ומתו שניהם באותה אדמה ונקברו דאי אפשר לו לעמוד בדין:
notes.en: But doesn’t Rav Ḥagga teach “and buried him”: that the ox buried the owner of the pit by its fall, knocking earth down on him, and both died in that earth and were buried; so it was impossible for him to stand trial. [Rabbeinu Gershom reads “Rav Ḥagga.”]

messages.text: The halakha in the baraita, that the owner of the ox collects from the heirs of the digger, is dealing with a case where judges sat at the opening of the pit and rendered the digger liable to pay damages before he died.
messages.quote: his heirs have to pay damages to the owner of the ox

notes.he: הא דקתני יורשין חייבין כגון דייתבי דייני אפומא דבירא וחייבוהו מיד לשלם:
notes.en: And the halakha: that which it teaches, that the heirs are liable, is for example where the judges sat at the opening of the pit and obligated him to pay at once.

notes.he: ומ"מ איצטריך למימר מת וקברו דס"ד דבעינן יבא בעל השור ויעמוד על שורו (סנהדרין דף יט.) קמ"ל דשפיר עמד עליה:
notes.en: Where the judges sat at the opening of the pit: and even so it was necessary to say “died and buried him,” since you might have thought that we require “Let the owner of the ox come and stand by his ox” (Sanhedrin 19a) [i.e., that the party must be present at the trial]; it teaches us that he properly stood by it.

notes.he: יורשין חייבין]:
notes.en: The halakha: [that] the heirs are liable.

notes.he: לעולם לאו ככתובה בשטר והכא אמאי יורשין חייבין כגון דייתבי דייני אפומא דבירא דחייבוהו קודם שתצא נשמתו לאלתר:
notes.en: Actually it is not like one written in a document; so here, why are the heirs liable? For example, where judges sat at the opening of the pit and obligated him immediately, before his soul departed.

messages.text: With regard to one taken to be executed, they sprinkle for his sake on the altar from the blood of his sin offering and from the blood of his guilt offering, which he brought earlier.
messages.lead: § The Sages taught another baraita on the same topic:

notes.he: זורקין בשבילו דם חטאתו ואשמו ולא הויא כחטאת שמתו בעליה כל זמן שלא נהרג:
notes.en: They sprinkle for him: they sprinkle on his behalf the blood of his sin offering and his guilt offering; and it is not like a sin offering whose owner has died, as long as he has not been executed.

notes.dh: מזין עליו מדם חטאתו ומדם אשמו
notes.he: דאין חטאת [ואשם] קריבה לאחר מיתתו אבל עולתו קריבה:
notes.en: They sprinkle for him from the blood of his sin offering and from the blood of his guilt offering: [it names these] since a sin offering and a guilt offering are not sacrificed after the owner’s death, but his burnt offering is sacrificed.

notes.he: על המזבח:
notes.en: They sprinkle for him: on the altar.

notes.he: שאם חטא קודם לכן והפריש קרבן ואח"כ נגמר דינו מזין עליו מדם חטאתו קודם שיהרג כדי שיתכפר על אותו חטא:
notes.en: From the blood of his sin offering: if he sinned before that and set aside an offering, and afterward his sentence was concluded, they sprinkle for him from the blood of his sin offering before he is executed, so that he gains atonement for that sin.

messages.text: But if he sinned at that time, obligating him to bring a sin offering or a guilt offering, the court does not attend to his obligation, and his execution is not delayed so that he can sacrifice the offering.

notes.he: בשוגג באותה שעה שיצא ליהרג כגון שראה חלב וכסבור שומן הוא ואכלו:
notes.en: Sinned: unwittingly, at the time that he went out to be executed; for example, he saw forbidden fat and thought it was permitted fat, and ate it.

notes.he: שיפריש קרבן ליקרב:
notes.en: One does not attend to him: [to wait] for him to set aside an offering to be sacrificed.

notes.he: שיוצא ליהרג אין נזקקין לו שיתכפר על אותו חטא:
notes.en: Sinned at that time: when he goes out to be executed, one does not attend to him so that he gain atonement for that sin.

messages.text: What is the reason for this?
messages.quote: the court does not attend to his obligation

messages.text: It is because the court may not afflict him by forcing him to wait for his judgment, his execution, until the offering is sacrificed.
messages.quote: What is the reason

notes.he: שימתינו מלהורגו עד שישחטו הזבח ויזרק הדם שעינוי הדין הוא:
notes.en: Because one does not afflict his judgment: [by] waiting to execute him until they slaughter the offering and the blood is sprinkled, for that is affliction of judgment.

notes.dh: [חטא באותה שעה שיוצא ליהרג אין נזקקין לו לעכבו עד שיפריש חטאתו
notes.he: שאין מענין דינו עד שישחט ויזרק:
notes.en: [Sinned at that time when he goes out to be executed: one does not attend to him, to hold him back until he sets aside his sin offering.] Because one does not afflict his judgment [by waiting] until it is slaughtered and [the blood] sprinkled.

messages.text: @Rav Yosef If so, if the offering is not sacrificed in order to avoid afflicting the sentenced by delaying his execution, then this should apply even in the first clause as well, where he had already brought the offering. Why does the court delay his execution until the blood is sprinkled?
messages.quote: may not afflict him

notes.he: דקתני כשחטא קודם לכן מזין עליו הרי ממתינים לו עד שישחט ויזרק:
notes.en: The first clause as well: which teaches that where he sinned before that, they sprinkle for him; there they do wait for him until it is slaughtered and [the blood] sprinkled.

messages.text: The first clause is referring to a case where his offering was already slaughtered at that time, and all that remained to be done was the sprinkling of the blood. Delaying the execution for such a short time is not a problem.
messages.quote: even in the first clause as well

notes.he: חטאתו:
notes.en: His offering slaughtered: his sin offering.

messages.text: But then in a case where he set aside his offering but it was not yet slaughtered, what is the halakha? Is it true that they do not delay his execution in order to sacrifice the offering?
messages.quote: where his offering was already slaughtered at that time

messages.text: If so, instead of teaching a new case and stating: But if he sinned at that time and thereby became obligated to sacrifice a sin offering or a guilt offering, the court does not attend to his obligation, let the baraita distinguish and teach a distinction within the case of where he already brought the offering itself:
In what case is this statement, that the blood is sprinkled, said? When his offering was already slaughtered at that time. But if his offering was not yet slaughtered, his execution is not delayed.

That is indeed what he is saying: In what case is this statement said? When his offering was already slaughtered at that time. But if his offering was not yet slaughtered, it is considered as though he sinned at that time, and therefore the court does not attend to his obligation.
Mishna
In the case of a pregnant woman who is taken by the court to be executed, the court does not wait to execute her until she gives birth. Rather, she is killed immediately.

notes.dh: מתני' אין ממתינין לה עד שתלד
notes.he: אלא הורגין ולדה עמה דחד גופא הוא:
notes.en: Mishna: One does not wait for her until she gives birth: rather, one executes her offspring with her, since it is one body.

notes.he: מעוברת היוצאה ליהרג אין ממתינין לה עד שתלד אלא ממיתין אותה עם ולדה דעובר כגופה הוא:
notes.en: The woman: a pregnant woman who goes out to be executed. One does not wait for her until she gives birth; rather, one puts her to death with her offspring, since the fetus is like her body.

messages.text: But with regard to a woman taken to be executed who sat on the travailing chair [hamashber] in the throes of labor, the court waits to execute her until she gives birth.

notes.he: קודם שנגמר דינה:
notes.en: Sat on the travailing chair: before her sentence was concluded.

notes.he: דכיון דעקר ונע ממקומו גופא אחרינא הוא:
notes.en: One waits for her until she gives birth: since once it has uprooted and moved from its place, it is another body.

notes.he: פרש"י קודם שנגמר דינה וליתא דאיוצא ליהרג קאי וכל היוצא ליהרג לאחר גמר דין כדמשמע בכל הנהו דמדכר לעיל במתני' בשמעתין וכן משמע בפ' כל הגט (גיטין דף כח:) דמדבר ביוצא לידון ויוצא ליהרג והיינו טעמא דרישא דאין ממתינין משום עינוי הדין (כלל) כדמשמע פרק אחד דיני ממונות (סנהדרין דף לה.) דליכא עינוי הדין אלא לאחר גמר דין מדקאמר היכי ליעביד לדייניה במעלי שבתא ולגמר דיניה בשבתא וליקטליה בחד בשבתא נמצא אתה מענה את דינו וכו' ליגמר דיניה בחד בשבתא קא מנשו לטעמייהו ולעינוי לא חיישינן:
notes.en: Sat on the travailing chair, etc.: Rashi explained: before her sentence was concluded. But this is not so, since it refers to one going out to be executed, and every “one going out to be executed” is after the conclusion of the sentence, as is implied in all those cases mentioned above in the mishna in our discussion; and so it is implied in chapter Kol HaGet (Gittin 28b), which speaks of “one going out to be judged” and “one going out to be executed.” And this is the reason of the first clause, that one does not wait, because of affliction of judgment; as is implied in chapter Eḥad Dinei Mamonot (Sanhedrin 35a), that there is affliction of judgment only after the conclusion of the sentence, since it says: How should one act? Let them judge him on Shabbat eve, conclude his sentence on Shabbat and execute him on Sunday? You are then found to afflict his judgment, etc. Let them conclude his sentence on Sunday? They will forget their reasons. [It is concerned there about forgetting,] and about affliction [before the sentence is concluded] we are not concerned.

messages.text: In the case of a woman who was killed through court-imposed capital punishment, one may derive benefit from her hair.

notes.he: ובגמ' מפרש טעמא:
notes.en: One may derive benefit from her hair: and the Gemara explains the reason.

messages.text: But in the case of an animal that was killed through court-imposed execution, e.g., for goring a person, deriving benefit from the animal is prohibited.

notes.he: כדקי"ל (פסחים דף כב:) ובעל השור נקי כאדם שאומר לחבירו יצא פלוני נקי מנכסיו ואין לו בהן הנאה של כלום:
notes.en: Is forbidden for benefit: as we maintain (Pesaḥim 22b) [from] “And the owner of the ox shall be clear” [Exodus 21:28], like a person who says to his fellow: So-and-so has gone out clear of his property, and has no benefit of any kind from it.

messages.text: Gemara
Isn’t it obvious that the court executes the pregnant woman rather than waiting? After all, it is part of her body.
messages.quote: does not wait to execute her until she gives birth

messages.text: It was necessary for the mishna to teach this, as it might enter your mind to say that since it is written: “And if men strive together, and hurt a woman with child, so that her offspring depart…he shall be fined, as the woman’s husband shall place upon him” (Exodus 21:22), the fetus is considered to be the property of the husband.

verse.he: וְכִי־יִנָּצוּ אֲנָשִׁים וְנָגְפוּ אִשָּׁה הָרָה וְיָצְאוּ יְלָדֶיהָ וְלֹא יִהְיֶה אָסוֹן עָנוֹשׁ יֵעָנֵשׁ כַּאֲשֶׁר יָשִׁית עָלָיו בַּעַל הָאִשָּׁה וְנָתַן בִּפְלִלִים׃
verse.en: When [two or more] parties fight, and one of them pushes a pregnant woman and a miscarriage results, but no other damage ensues, [the one responsible] shall be fined according as the woman’s husband may exact, the payment to be based on reckoning.

notes.he: הוולדות]:
notes.en: It is the husband’s property: the offspring.

messages.text: If so, the court should wait until she gives birth before executing her, and not cause him to lose the fetus. Consequently, the mishna teaches us that the court does not take this factor into account.
But why not say that indeed the court should delay her execution until she gives birth?

The verse states: “If a man be found lying with a woman married to a husband, then they shall also both of them die, the man that lay with the woman, and the woman” (Deuteronomy 22:22). The amplifying term “both of them” serves to add her fetus, teaching that it dies together with her.
messages.quote: why not say that indeed the court should delay her execution

verse.he: כִּי־יִמָּצֵא אִישׁ שֹׁכֵב ׀ עִם־אִשָּׁה בְעֻלַת־בַּעַל וּמֵתוּ גַּם־שְׁנֵיהֶם הָאִישׁ הַשֹּׁכֵב עִם־הָאִשָּׁה וְהָאִשָּׁה וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל׃ {ס}
verse.en: If a man is found lying with another man’s wife, both of them—the man and the woman with whom he lay—shall die. Thus you will sweep away evil from Israel.

notes.he: קס"ד משניהם יליף מדה"ל למיכתב ומתו ואנא ידענא דאין ומתו פחות משנים:
notes.en: Gemara: To include the offspring: it was assumed that he derives it from “both of them,” since it could have written “and they shall die,” and I would know that “and they shall die” means no fewer than two.

notes.he: שניהם מיותר לדרשה:
notes.en: “Both of them” is superfluous, [and therefore available] for exposition.

messages.text: But this phrase is required for the following halakha: Neither of the two adulterers mentioned in the verse is punished until both of them are equal, i.e., they have both reached majority. This is the statement of Rabbi Yoshiya.
messages.quote: both of them

notes.he: הנואף והנואפת יהו בני עונשין אבל אם היתה היא קטנה והוא גדול או הוא קטן דלאו בר עונשין והיא גדולה ובת עונשין אין הגדול נהרג: ומשני אנו מגם ילפינן:
notes.en: Both of them equal: the adulterer and the adulteress must both be subject to punishment. But if she was a minor and he an adult, or he a minor, who is not subject to punishment, and she an adult and subject to punishment, the adult is not executed. And the Gemara answers: we derive [the fetus] from “also.”

notes.he: מזידין. [אבל אם אחד מהן שוגג] או שאם היתה היא (ילדה) [קטנה] והוא גדול אינו נהרג:
notes.en: Until both of them are equal: [both] intentional. [But if one of them was unwitting,] or if she was a minor and he an adult, he is not executed.

messages.text: When you say that the child also dies, it is derived from the word “also,” whereas the halakha that they must be equal is learned from the term “both of them.”
messages.quote: until both of them are equal

notes.he: כי קא מרבינן לוולד מגם:
notes.en: That is derived from “also”: when we include the offspring, it is from “also.”

messages.text: § What is the reason for delaying the execution in this case?
messages.quote: who sat on the travailing chair

messages.text: Once the fetus uproots from its place and begins to leave the woman’s body, it is considered an independent body and may not be killed together with the mother.

notes.he: לצאת]:
notes.en: Once it has uprooted: to come out.

messages.text: In the case of a pregnant woman who is taken by the court to be executed, one strikes her opposite the womb, i.e., on the abdomen, so that the fetus dies first and so that she not suffer disgrace as a result of publicly bleeding from labor.

notes.he: שאם יהא חיות בולד יצא לאחר מיתת אמו וניוול הוא:
notes.en: Disgrace: for if there is life in the offspring, it will come out after its mother’s death, and that is a disgrace.

notes.he: שאם היה העובר חי לאחר מיתת אמו היה מפרכס ויוצא והיתה שופעת דם מאותו מקום ותתנוול בפני הכל הילכך מכין אותה בבטן כנגד הוולד:
notes.en: So that she not come to disgrace: for if the fetus were alive after its mother’s death, it would move convulsively and come out, and she would stream blood from that place and be disgraced before everyone. Therefore they strike her on the abdomen, opposite the offspring.

messages.text: Is this to say that according to Shmuel if a pregnant woman dies, she dies first, before the fetus? It is clear that this is Shmuel’s assumption, as he mandates killing the fetus before the mother, lest the live fetus bring about the onset of labor as a reaction to the woman’s death. Were the fetus to perish first, before the woman, there would be no need for this.
messages.quote: so that the fetus dies first

messages.text: But this is difficult, as we maintain that the fetus dies first.
A baby boy, one day old, inherits the estate of his relatives who died on the day of his birth, and if he dies, he bequeaths that inheritance to his relatives.

notes.he: אם נפלה לו ירושה בו ביום ובו ביום מת מנחילה לקרוביו מאביו:
notes.en: Inherits: if an inheritance fell to him on that day, and he died that same day, he bequeaths it to his relatives on his father’s side.

notes.he: שמתה אמו כשילדתו והתינוק מת למחר:
notes.en: A day-old baby: whose mother died when she bore him, and the baby died the next day.

messages.text: This mishna is teaching that a day-old child inherits his mother’s property when she died after he was born, to bequeath it to his heirs who are not the mother’s heirs, e.g., to his paternal brothers.
messages.quote: A baby boy, one day old, inherits

notes.he: האי נוחל ומנחיל ליכא לאוקומי בנכסי אביו דא"נ לא אתיליד איהו הוו ירתי קרוביו נכסי אביו היכא דאין בנים:
notes.en: And Rav Sheshet said: this “inherits and bequeaths” cannot be explained as referring to his father’s property, since even had he not been born, his relatives would inherit his father’s property, where there are no sons [so his inheriting would change nothing].

notes.he: אם מתה בו ביום ואפי' הוא מת בו ביום נוחל נכסי אמו ומנחילן מכחו לאחיו מאביו שאינן בני אמו דאי לאו הוא הוו ירתי לה קרוביה ולא אמרי' נפל הוא ואינו בן נחלה:
notes.en: Rather, he inherits his mother’s property: if she died on that day; and even if he died on that day, he inherits his mother’s property and passes it on, through his own right, to his brothers from his father who are not his mother’s sons; for were it not for him, her own relatives would inherit her. And we do not say that he is a stillborn [nefel] and not fit to inherit.

notes.he: נוחל בנכסי האם להנחיל לאחיו מן האב. שאם הוא מאם אחת ואחיו מאם אחרת וירש הוא מאמו נכסים מנחיל לאחין מן האב דאחין מן האב יורשין זה את זה:
notes.en: Inherits and bequeaths: he inherits his mother’s property, to bequeath it to his brothers from the father. For if he is from one mother and his brothers from another mother, and he inherited property from his mother, he bequeaths it to the brothers from the father, since paternal brothers inherit one another.

messages.text: It is specifically in a case where the boy is one day old that he inherits and bequeaths, but a fetus who died while still in the womb does not inherit and bequeath. The reason is that we presume that the fetus died first, before its mother, and a son does not inherit through his mother while in the grave, in order to bequeath her property to his paternal brothers.

notes.he: אם מתה מעוברת לא ירתי לה קרובי העובר דהוא מת ברישא:
notes.en: But a fetus: if she died while pregnant, the fetus’s relatives do not inherit her, since it dies first.

notes.he: כלומר שמתה אמו ולא נולד אין אחין נוחלין נחלת אמו דהוא מיית ברישא בבטן אמו קודם אמו ואין הבן יורש את אמו בקבר מאחר שמת קודם אמו להנחיל לאחין מן האב אלמא דעובר מיית ברישא דאי איהי מתה ברישא לירתה ולירתינהו לאחי]:
notes.en: But a fetus, no: that is, where its mother died and it was not born, the brothers do not inherit its mother’s estate, since it dies first in its mother’s womb, before its mother; and a son does not inherit his mother in the grave, having died before her, to bequeath to the brothers from the father. Evidently the fetus dies first; for if she died first, let it inherit her and let the brothers inherit from it.

messages.text: This matter, i.e., the presumption that the fetus dies first, applies only in a case of natural death. In such a situation, since the fetus’s vitality is minimal, the Angel of Death’s drop of poison enters his body and cuts the two organs that must be severed in ritual slaughter, i.e., the windpipe and the gullet [simanim], thereby killing him before his mother.
messages.quote: she dies first, before the fetus

notes.he: דהוא מיית ברישא לגבי מיתה כשהיא מתה מיתת עצמה:
notes.en: And the Gemara answers: this applies, that it dies first, with regard to death, when she dies her own death.

notes.he: טיפה של מרה:
notes.en: The drop of the Angel of Death: a drop of gall.

messages.text: But in a case where the mother was killed, e.g., if she was executed, she dies first.
Is it true that the fetus always dies first when the mother dies naturally? But there was an incident where the mother died naturally and the fetus made three spasmodic motions afterward.
messages.quote: applies only in a case of natural death

notes.he: ופרכינן וגבי מיתה מי מיית הוא ברישא והא הוה עובדא ופרכיס לאחר מיתת אמו:
notes.en: And we object: with regard to [natural] death, does it really die first? But there was an incident, and it moved convulsively after its mother’s death.

notes.he: ניענע עצמו ג' פעמים העובר אחר שמתה אמו:
notes.en: And it made three convulsions: the fetus moved itself three times after its mother died.

messages.text: That is just as it is with the tail of the lizard, which jerks after being severed from the lizard; it is just a spasmodic motion, which does not indicate that it is still alive.
messages.quote: made three spasmodic motions

notes.he: אם חותכין אותה מפרכסת החתיכה ואע"פ שאין בה חיות:
notes.en: The tail of the lizard: if one cuts it off, the cut piece moves convulsively even though there is no life in it.

notes.he: לאו פירכוס דאית ביה חיות הוא אלא הוי כזנב הלטאה שמפרכסת אחר שנחתך הזנב ממנה ופרכס הזנב:
notes.en: That convulsion: it is not a convulsion that has life in it; rather, it is like the lizard’s tail, which moves convulsively after the tail is cut from it.

messages.text: § In the case of a woman who sat on the travailing chair in the throes of labor, and died on Shabbat, one brings a knife, and tears open her abdomen, and removes the fetus, as it might still be alive, and it could be possible to save its life.

notes.he: דזימנין דמיקרי דהיא מייתא ברישא:
notes.en: And one tears open her abdomen: since it sometimes happens that she dies first.

messages.text: But isn’t it obvious that this is permitted? After all, what is the person who cuts her abdomen doing?
messages.quote: one brings a knife, and tears open her abdomen

messages.text: 7b
It is merely cutting flesh, and there is no reason why it should be prohibited.

notes.he: ואין חיוב אלא בחובל בחי דמוציא דם:
notes.en: It is merely cutting flesh: and there is liability [for wounding on Shabbat] only for one who wounds a living creature, drawing blood.

notes.he: כלומר כיון דמתה לית (לן) בה משום חבורה:
notes.en: It is cutting flesh: that is, since she has died, there is no [prohibition of] wounding in her.

messages.text: No, the halakha concerning cutting open her abdomen is necessary only to teach that it is permitted to bring a knife by way of the public thoroughfare for that purpose, despite the fact that this constitutes a prohibited labor by Torah law.
messages.quote: isn’t it obvious that this is permitted

messages.text: And what does this teach us? Does it teach that even in a case of uncertainty we desecrate Shabbat for the chance of saving a life? But we already learned this in a mishna:
messages.quote: to bring a knife by way of the public thoroughfare

messages.text: With regard to one upon whom a rockslide fell, and there is uncertainty as to whether he is there under the debris or whether he is not there, and there is also uncertainty as to whether he is still alive or whether he is dead, and finally there is uncertainty as to whether the person under the debris is a gentile or a Jew, one clears the pile from atop him on Shabbat.

It is necessary to teach that one may bring a knife in the case of a woman, lest you say that it is specifically there that one may desecrate Shabbat, as the person who was buried under the rockslide had a presumptive status of being alive and therefore he is assumed to still be alive.
messages.quote: one clears the pile from atop him

messages.text: But here, where the child had no prior presumptive status of being alive, as he was not yet born, you might say that one may not desecrate Shabbat in order to save his life. Therefore, it is necessary for Shmuel to teach us that even here one may desecrate Shabbat for the possibility of saving the fetus’s life.
§ But why is it permitted? After all, a corpse and its hair are items from which deriving benefit is prohibited.
messages.quote: a woman who was killed

notes.he: כדתרצינן מבעל השור נקי:
notes.en: An animal that was killed is forbidden for benefit: as we explained from “The owner of the ox shall be clear” [Exodus 21:28].

notes.he: דיליף שם שם מעגלה ערופה:
notes.en: They are items forbidden for benefit: a corpse, as one derives “there” from “there” from the heifer whose neck is broken.

messages.text: This is referring to a case where she says before she dies: Give my hair to my daughter.
messages.quote: But why is it permitted

messages.text: Is the prohibition contingent on the deceased’s wishes? Were she to say: Give my hand to my daughter, would we give the hand to her?
messages.quote: Give my hair to my daughter

messages.text: Rather, this is not referring to the actual hair of the deceased, but to a wig [pe’a nokhrit], which is not part of the deceased’s body.

notes.he: רגילות היו נשים כששערן מועט לקשור שיער נשים נכריות לשערן והוא פיאה נכרית):
notes.en: (One may derive benefit from her hair: women whose hair was sparse were accustomed to tie the hair of other women to their own hair, and that is a pe’a nokhrit.)

notes.he: קליעה:
notes.en: Pe’a: a braid.

notes.he: לאו שערה ממש קאמר אלא שהיתה לה פיאה משיער אשה אחרת קשורה לשערה [דרגילות היו נשים כששערן מועט לקשור שיער נשים נכריות לשערן והוא פיאה נכרית] ואמרה תנו אותה לבתי וקמ"ל מתני' דאע"ג דקשורה לה כיון דאמרה תנו גליא דעתה דלא ניחא לה דתיהוי כגופה לאיתסורי בהדיה וכנטולה מחיים דמיא:
notes.en: With a wig: he does not mean her actual hair, but that she had a wig of another woman’s hair tied to her hair [for women whose hair was sparse were accustomed to tie the hair of other women to their own hair, and that is a pe’a nokhrit], and she said: Give it to my daughter. And the mishna teaches us that even though it is tied to her, since she said “Give,” she revealed her mind that she does not want it to be like her body, so as to become forbidden along with it; and it is like something removed during her lifetime.

notes.he: שער של אשה אחרת שלא היתה מחוברת לשערה ואותו שער מותר בהנאה:
notes.en: With a wig: the hair of another woman that was not attached to her hair; and that hair is permitted for benefit.

messages.text: The reason it is permitted is that she said to give her wig to her daughter, thereby indicating that she did not consider it part of her body. But if she did not say to give her wig to her daughter, it is considered part of her body, and it is forbidden to derive benefit from it.
messages.quote: to a wig

messages.text: But didn’t Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, raise this as a dilemma?

With regard to the hair of righteous women in a city whose residents were incited to idolatry and, therefore, all of their property must be burned, what is the halakha? Is it considered their property and burned, or part of their body and not burned?
messages.lead: As Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina raised a dilemma:

notes.he: של עיר הנדחת שלא הודחו עמה מהו ואמר רבא התם בחלק (סנהדרין קיב.) פיאה נכרית שקשרה הצדקת לשערה קא מיבעיא ליה אי כגופה היא וניצול אי כממונה וקי"ל (שם) צדיקים שבתוכה יוצאין ממנה ערומים וכל ממונם נשרף דכתיב ואת כל שללה תקבוץ וגו' אלמא מספקא ליה אי כגופה אי לאו כגופה ותיפשוט ליה מהכא דגופה הוא דטעמא דאמרה תנו כו':
notes.en: The hair of righteous women: of an idolatrous city, who were not led astray along with it: what is [the law]? And Rava said there, in chapter Ḥelek (Sanhedrin 112a): he asks about a wig that the righteous woman tied to her hair, whether it is like her body and is saved, or like her property. And we maintain (there) that the righteous within it go out of it naked and all their property is burned, as it is written: “And you shall gather all its spoil,” etc. [Deuteronomy 13:17]. Evidently he is uncertain whether it is like her body or not; so let him resolve it from here that it is her body, since the reason is that she said “Give,” etc.

messages.text: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, was not referring to actual hair, but rather he raised his dilemma with regard to a wig.
messages.quote: hair of righteous women

messages.text: This is difficult according to the opinion of Rav, as his ruling indicates that a wig should be considered part of a woman’s body unless she stipulated otherwise.

When Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, raised his dilemma as to whether a wig is considered part of the body, he was referring specifically to a case where the wig was hanging on a peg. The dilemma is whether it is considered part of her clothing, which, like her body, is not burned, or whether it is considered like any other property of hers, since she was not wearing it at the time.

notes.he: של עיר הנדחת דאמרי' התם צדיקים שבתוכה גופן פלט וממונם אבד ואמר רבא בפאה נכרית קא מיבעיא ליה אי הוי כממון ולא גופה הוא או דילמא כיון דמחבר ליה הוי כגופה. ודאי] אי מחובר לה. לא קא מיבעיא ליה דודאי כגופה ופלט כי קא מיבעיא ליה דתלי [הפאה] בסיכתא:
notes.en: The hair of righteous women: of an idolatrous city, for we say there that the righteous within it, their bodies escape and their property is lost. And Rava said he asks about a wig: whether it is like property and not her body, or perhaps, since it is attached to her, it is like her body. Certainly, if it is attached to her, he does not ask, since certainly it is like her body and escapes; when he asks, it is where [the wig] is hanging on a peg.

messages.text: On the other hand, here Rav is referring to a wig that is actually attached to her. In such a case, one may correctly infer that the reason that it is permitted is that the deceased said to give her wig to her daughter, thereby indicating that she did not consider it part of her body. But if she did not say to give her wig to her daughter, it is considered to be part of her body and is prohibited.

notes.he: הוי כמופרש ממנה:
notes.en: The reason is that she said “Give”: it is like something separated from her.

messages.text: The mishna teaches the issue of the prohibition of the woman’s hair as being similar to the other prohibition it mentions, that of the animal. Just as there, in the case of the animal, it is referring to deriving benefit from its body, so too here, it must be referring to benefit from her body itself, not from a wig.
messages.lead: This claim, that the mishna is dealing with a wig rather than natural hair, is difficult for Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak.
messages.quote: to a wig

notes.he: הא דמוקמינן למתניתין בפיאה נכרית והא דומיא דבהמה קתני וכו':
notes.en: It is difficult for Rav Naḥman: [namely,] that we explained the mishna as referring to a wig; but it teaches it as similar to an animal, etc. [Rashi’s heading reads “Rav Naḥman.”]

notes.he: דבהמה אין לה פאה נכרית אף הכא באשה בשערה דגופה קא מיירי ולא בפאה נכרית:
notes.en: Just as there, its body: since an animal has no wig, so too here, with a woman, it is speaking of the hair of her body and not of a wig.

messages.text: The Aramaic of the next line names only “Rav Naḥman”; the lines around it attribute this view to Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak.

the mishna is referring to natural hair, and there is a distinction between the hair of an animal and that of a woman. In the case of this woman, it is her death that causes her to be forbidden. Therefore, the hair, which does not undergo any change when she dies, remains permitted.

notes.he: לעולם שערה ממש ודקשיא לך איסורי הנאה נינהו ל"ק דשיער המת לא מיתסר בהנאה דלא דמי לשיער בהמה שנהרגה דאשה מיתתה אוסרתה ושיער לאו בר מיתה הוא שאין עשוי להשתנות אבל בהמה גמר דינה אוסרתה כדאמר בפסחים בפ' כל שעה (פסחים דף כב:) ממשמע שנאמר סקל יסקל השור איני יודע שהוא נבילה ואסורה באכילה ומה ת"ל לא יאכל את בשרו מגיד שאם שחטו לאחר גמר דינו אסור ואין לי אלא באכילה בהנאה מנין כו' והילכך כל דמחובר בה בשעת גמר דין מיתסר בהדה:
notes.en: Rather, Rav Naḥman said: actually it is her real hair. And as for your difficulty, that these are forbidden for benefit: it is not difficult, since the hair of a corpse is not forbidden for benefit. It is not like the hair of an animal that was killed, since a woman, her death forbids her, and hair is not subject to death, since it does not change; but an animal, the conclusion of its sentence forbids it, as it says in Pesaḥim, chapter Kol Sha’a (Pesaḥim 22b): From the implication of that which is stated, “The ox shall surely be stoned” [Exodus 21:28], do I not know that it is an unslaughtered carcass and forbidden to be eaten? Why then does the verse state, “And its flesh shall not be eaten”? It tells you that if one slaughtered it after its sentence was concluded, it is forbidden. And I have [derived] only [the prohibition of] eating; from where [do I derive] benefit? etc. Therefore whatever is attached to it at the time the sentence is concluded becomes forbidden with it.

notes.he: היינו טעמא דנהנין בשערה דזו אשה מיתתה אוסרתה דאפי' אינה נהרגת [אלא] מתה כדרכה נאסרת בהנאה וכי קא אסרה מידי דהוי גופה ממש דמשתנה מחמת מיתה שערה אינה משתנה הילכך כי אמרה קודם מיתה תנו הוי כמופרש ממנה ונהנין:
notes.en: Rather, Rav Naḥman said: this is the reason one may derive benefit from her hair: this woman, her death forbids her, for even if she is not executed but dies naturally, she becomes forbidden for benefit. And what it forbids is that which is her actual body, which changes because of death; her hair does not change. Therefore, when she said before her death “Give,” it is like something separated from her, and one may derive benefit from it.

messages.text: But in the case of that animal, the verdict causes it to be forbidden, even before it is killed. It is prohibited to derive benefit from the animal as soon as the verdict is issued. Therefore, the hair that is attached to the animal is forbidden as well.

notes.he: בהמה:
notes.en: And this: an animal.

notes.he: בהנאה ולא מיתתה הילכך משעה שנגמר דינה [נגמר דינה אכולה] אגופה ואשערה הילכך אין נהנין בשערה:
notes.en: The conclusion of its sentence forbids it: for benefit, and not its death. Therefore, from the time its sentence was concluded, [the sentence applied to all of it,] to its body and to its hair; therefore one may not derive benefit from its hair.

messages.text: Levi teaches a baraita in accordance with the opinion of Rav, and Levi also teaches a baraita in accordance with the opinion of Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak.

notes.he: דמוקים לה בדאמרה תנו ובפיאה נכרית:
notes.en: Levi teaches in accordance with Rav: who explains it as where she said “Give,” and as referring to a wig.

messages.text: In the case of a woman who was being taken to be killed and who said: Give my hair to my daughter, one gives it to the daughter. If she died without instructing that it be given to her daughter, one does not give it to the daughter, because it is forbidden to derive benefit from a corpse.
messages.lead: Levi teaches a baraita in accordance with the opinion of Rav:

notes.he: ולא אמרה תנו אין נותנין כו':
notes.en: Died: and did not say “Give”: one does not give, etc.

notes.he: דכתיב ותמת שם מרים וגמר שם שם מעגלה ערופה במסכת ע"ז באין מעמידין (ע"ז דף כט:):
notes.en: A corpse is forbidden for benefit: as it is written: “And Miriam died there” [Numbers 20:1], and one derives “there” from “there” in [the passage of] the heifer whose neck is broken [Deuteronomy 21:4], in tractate Avoda Zara, chapter Ein Ma’amidin (Avoda Zara 29b).

messages.text: Isn’t it obvious that this is the reason her hair is prohibited? This is referring not to the hair itself, but rather to a wig, and the baraita is teaching that it is forbidden to derive benefit even from the adornments of the deceased, such as a wig.
messages.quote: because it is forbidden to derive benefit from a corpse

notes.he: דמש"ה אין נותנין שהמת אסור בהנאה אלא ודאי ה"ק שנויי המת כגון פיאה נכרית אסורין בהנאה ולהכי קתני להאי מפני משום דקא בעי לגלויי עלה דלאו בשערה ממש קא מיירי:
notes.en: Obvious: that one does not give for this reason, since a corpse is forbidden for benefit. Rather, certainly this is what it is saying: the adornments of the dead, such as a wig, are forbidden for benefit. And that is why it teaches this “because,” since it wants to reveal that it is not dealing with her actual hair.

notes.he: אלמא בפאה נכרית קא מיירי:
notes.en: The adornments of the dead are forbidden for benefit: evidently it is dealing with a wig.

messages.text: Whereas in the case of a woman who died, one may derive benefit from her hair, with regard to an animal that was put to death, it is forbidden to derive benefit from it.
messages.lead: It is taught in a baraita in accordance with the opinion of Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak, as follows:

notes.he: אפי' שערה:
notes.en: An animal that was killed is forbidden for benefit: even its hair.

notes.he: ותניא כותיה דרב נחמן דבשערה דגופה ממש קא מיירי:
notes.en: And it is taught in accordance with Rav Naḥman, that it is dealing with the actual hair of her body.

messages.text: And what is the difference between this case and that one? In this case it is her death that causes her to be forbidden, but in that case the verdict causes the animal to be forbidden.

notes.he: סליק פירקא
notes.en: The chapter is concluded.

messages.text: הדרן עלך הכל מעריכין · Hadran alakh HaKol Ma’arikhin: we will return to you, chapter 1, “Everyone Takes Vows of Valuation.”
Chapter 2 · אין נערכין · Ein Ne’erakhin: the least and the most, beginning with the smallest and largest sums a valuation can cost.
Mishna
One cannot be charged for a valuation less than a sela, nor can one be charged more than fifty sela.

notes.he: שאפי' עני הנדור בהשג יד לא יתן פחות מסלע:
notes.en: Mishna: One cannot be valuated for less than a sela: for even a poor man, who is judged according to his means, may not give less than a sela.

notes.he: דזהו גדול שבערכין הכתובין בפרשה:
notes.en: Nor more than fifty: for that is the largest of the valuations written in the passage.

notes.he: אין נוטלין לעולם מן המעריכין פחות מסלע ולא יותר על חמשים סלע:
notes.en: One cannot be valuated for less than a sela: one never takes from those who valuate less than a sela, nor more than fifty sela.

messages.text: How so? If one gave one sela and became wealthy, he is not required to give anything more, as he has fulfilled his obligation. If he gave less than a sela and became wealthy, he is required to give fifty sela, as he has not fulfilled his obligation.

notes.he: בן עשרים שערכו חמישים והיה עני ונתן סלע לערכו דעני נידון בהשג יד והעשיר פטור:
notes.en: He gave a sela: [for example,] a twenty-year-old, whose valuation is fifty, was poor and gave a sela for his valuation, since a poor man is judged according to his means; and [then] he became wealthy: he is exempt.

notes.he: דבנתינה קמייתא לא יצא ידי ערכו ועדיין ערכו עליו ועני המעריך את עצמו והעשיר קודם נתינה נותן ערך עשיר כדילפינן לקמן בפ' השג יד (ערכין דף יז:):
notes.en: He gives fifty: since with the first giving he did not fulfill [the obligation of] his valuation, and his valuation is still upon him. And a poor man who valuated himself and became wealthy before giving gives the valuation of a wealthy man, as we derive below in chapter HaSeg Yad (Arakhin 17b).

notes.he: פחות מסלע והעשיר לאו דווקא פחות מסלע אלא אפי' נתן כל הערך חוץ מסלע אחד מגלגלין עליו את הכל:
notes.en: One cannot be valuated for less than a sela, etc.: “Less than a sela and became wealthy” is not specifically less than a sela; rather, even if he gave the entire valuation except for one sela, the whole is imposed upon him.

notes.he: אמר ערכי עלי חמשים סלע ולא היתה ידו משגת אלא לסלע אחד ונתנו נפטר מן הערך אע"פ שהעשיר אינו נותן כלום. אבל אם נתן פחות מסלע והעשיר נותן חמשים סלע]:
notes.en: [How so? He said: My valuation is upon me, fifty sela, and his means sufficed for only one sela, and he gave it: he is exempt from the valuation, and even if he became wealthy, he gives nothing. But if he gave less than a sela and became wealthy, he gives fifty sela.]

messages.text: If there were five sela in the possession of the destitute person, and the valuation he undertook is more than five sela, how much should he pay?

notes.he: עני בן עשרים שהעריך עצמו והיה לו ה' סלעים:
notes.en: There were five sela in his possession: a poor man of twenty who valuated himself and had five sela.

notes.he: וערכו היה חמשים:
notes.en: There were five sela in his possession: and his valuation was fifty.

messages.text: He gives only one sela and thereby fulfills his obligation.

notes.dh: ר' מאיר אומר אינו נותן אלא אחד
notes.he: הואיל ואין ידו משגת לכל הערך:
notes.en: Rabbi Meir says: he gives only one: since his means do not suffice for the whole valuation.

messages.text: He gives all five.
One cannot be charged for a valuation less than a sela; nor can one be charged more than fifty sela.
Gemara

From where do we derive this principle? As it is written: “And all your valuations shall be according to the shekel of the Sanctuary” (Leviticus 27:25). This verse indicates that all valuations that you valuate shall not be less than a shekel, which is the equivalent of a sela. One does not fulfill his obligation by giving less than this amount.
messages.quote: One cannot be charged for a valuation less than a sela

verse.he: וְכׇל־עֶרְכְּךָ יִהְיֶה בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ עֶשְׂרִים גֵּרָה יִהְיֶה הַשָּׁקֶל׃
verse.en: All assessments shall be by the sanctuary weight, the shekel being twenty gerahs.

notes.he: סתם לא יהו פחות משקל ואינו נפטר עד שיתן סלע שלם כדאמרינן לעיל דהא כתב שקל בערך המועט וכתיב חמשים בערך המרובה:
notes.en: All valuations that you valuate: in general, shall not be less than a shekel; and he is not exempt until he gives a whole sela, as we said above, since it wrote “shekel” for the small valuation and “fifty” for the large valuation.

messages.text: This is the highest valuation specified in the Torah, as it is written: “Then your valuation shall be for the male from twenty years old unto sixty years old, your valuation shall be fifty shekels of silver” (Leviticus 27:3).
messages.quote: nor can one be charged more than fifty sela

verse.he: וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ הַזָּכָר מִבֶּן עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה וְעַד בֶּן־שִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ חֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כֶּסֶף בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ׃
verse.en: the following scale shall apply: If it is a male from twenty to sixty years of age, the equivalent is fifty shekels of silver by the sanctuary weight;

messages.text: § What is the reason for the opinion of Rabbi Meir? It is written with regard to a male between the ages of twenty and sixty: “Your valuation shall be fifty shekels of silver” (Leviticus 27:3), and the verses likewise specify the valuations for other individuals.
messages.quote: If there were five sela in the possession

messages.text: And it is also written: “Your valuations shall be according to the shekel of the Sanctuary” (Leviticus 27:25). This teaches that the valuation is either fifty shekels for one who vows to donate the valuation of a man between twenty and sixty, or one shekel, if he cannot afford to pay fifty.
And how do the Rabbis respond to this reasoning?

According to the Rabbis, that second verse comes to teach that all valuations that you valuate shall not be less than a shekel, but in a case where the individual has more than a shekel, the verse states: “According to the means of him that vowed shall the priest value him” (Leviticus 27:8), and as he has the means to pay more than a shekel, he is required to pay the maximum that he can afford.

verse.he: וְאִם־מָךְ הוּא מֵעֶרְכֶּךָ וְהֶעֱמִידוֹ לִפְנֵי הַכֹּהֵן וְהֶעֱרִיךְ אֹתוֹ הַכֹּהֵן עַל־פִּי אֲשֶׁר תַּשִּׂיג יַד הַנֹּדֵר יַעֲרִיכֶנּוּ הַכֹּהֵן׃ {ס}
verse.en: But if someone cannot afford the equivalent, they shall be presented before the priest, and the priest shall make an assessment; the priest shall make the assessment according to what the vower can afford.

notes.dh: גמ' ההוא לכל ערכין שאתה מעריך הוא דאתא
notes.he: שאפי' עני שבעניים לא יתן פחות ומיהו היכא דאית ליה טפי יהיב דכתיב על פי אשר תשיג:
notes.en: Gemara: That one comes for all valuations that you valuate: that even the poorest of the poor may not give less. But where he has more, he gives, as it is written: “according to the means.”

notes.he: יהיב מה דאית ליה דכתיב אשר תשיג יד הנודר:
notes.en: [Where he has: he gives what he has, as it is written: “according to the means of him that vowed.”

messages.text: And how does Rabbi Meir respond to this reasoning? According to Rabbi Meir, that verse comes to teach that the charge is calculated according to the means of one who took the vow and not according to the means of the one about whom the vow was made. Consequently, if a poor man vowed to donate the valuation of a rich man, the amount to be paid is calculated according to what the poor man, not the rich man, can afford.

notes.he: שעני שהעריך את העשיר נותן ערך עני:
notes.en: The means of the one who vows and not the means of the one vowed: that a poor man who valuated a rich man gives the valuation of a poor man.

notes.dh: ההוא יד הנודר ולא יד הנידר
notes.he: ואם תאמר מה לי לרבויי נידר דאיצטריך קרא למעוטי וי"ל כיון דכתיב קרא (חמשים) (ויקרא כ״ז:כ״ה) וכל ערכך יהיה בשקל הקדש דלא יהא ערך פחות משקל ואשכחן ערך חמשים ס"ד דהאי טעמא משום השג יד ידעינן מסברא ואזלינן בתר הנידר קמ"ל קרא דאשר תשיג יד הנודר דלא אזלינן בתר הנידר:
notes.en: That one [comes for] the means of the one who vows and not the means of the one vowed: And if you say: what reason would there be to include the one vowed, that a verse was needed to exclude it? One can say: since the verse is written, “And all your valuations shall be according to the shekel of the Sanctuary” [Leviticus 27:25], [teaching] that a valuation shall not be less than a shekel, and we find a valuation of fifty, one might have thought that this matter, [reducing it] according to means, we know from reasoning, and [then] we would follow the one vowed. [So] the verse teaches us, “according to the means of him that vowed,” that we do not follow the one vowed.

notes.he: האי אשר תשיג יד הנודר אשר תשיג אתי למעוטי יד הנידר דעני שהעריך את העשיר נותן ערך עני מה שידו משגת ולא אזלינן בתר נידר]:
notes.en: And Rabbi Meir: this “according to the means of him that vowed” comes to exclude the means of the one vowed: that a poor man who valuated a rich man gives a poor man’s valuation, what his means suffice for, and we do not follow the one vowed.]

messages.text: And how do the Rabbis respond to this reasoning? They would say: Doesn’t it emerge by itself that you also learn from this verse that in a case where he has the means to pay more than a shekel, you should take from him the maximum that he can afford?

notes.he: אע"ג דקרא להכי אתא ולא יד הנידר מיהו על פי אשר תשיג כתיב וממילא שמעת דהיכא דידו משגת שקול מיניה:
notes.en: Don’t we learn from it by itself, etc.: even though the verse comes for this, “and not the means of the one vowed,” nevertheless “according to the means” is written, and by itself you learn that where his means suffice, take from him.

notes.he: כלומר דתרווייהו שמעת מינה [ש"מ] דיד הנודר ולא יד הנידר וש"מ מדאמר אשר תשיג דהיכא דידו משגת שקלינן מיניה כל מה שיש לו:
notes.en: And don’t [you learn from it, etc.]: that is, you learn both from it: the means of the one who vows and not of the one vowed; and learn from its saying “according to the means” that where his means suffice, we take from him all that he has.

messages.text: If one had five sela in his possession and said: It is incumbent upon me to donate my valuation, and he then said again: It is incumbent upon me to donate my valuation, and he gave four sela for the second vow and one sela for the first vow, he has fulfilled his obligation to pay for both of the vows. Consequently, even if he becomes wealthy, he is not required to make any further payments.
messages.lead: § The Gemara cites a ruling based upon the opinion of the Rabbis.

notes.he: על פי כהן יצא ידי שניהן ואפי' לרבנן הואיל ויהב לשניה ברישא:
notes.en: And he gave four for the second: by the priest’s [assessment], he fulfilled both of them, even according to the Rabbis, since he gave to the second first.

notes.he: לערך שנייה ואחת לראשונה:
notes.en: [And he gave four: for the second valuation, and one for the first.

messages.text: What is the reason for this? There is a principle that with regard to a creditor holding a promissory note dated later than the notes of other creditors, who collected his debt before the other creditors collected theirs, whatever he has collected he has collected, and it is not expropriated from him even if the debtor does not have the means to pay back all his creditors.
messages.quote: he has fulfilled his obligation to pay for both of the vows

notes.he: והילכך כי יהיב לראשונה כל מה דאית ליה יהיב לה ולשניה ליכא למימר אמאי לא יהב כולהו חמש משום דבעידנא דיהב לשניה משתעבד לה לראשונה דהא אפילו מאי דיהיב לה לאו דידה הוא:
notes.en: Whatever he has collected he has collected: and therefore when he gives to the first, he gives it all that he has. And regarding the second, one cannot say: Why did he not give all five? Because at the time that he gave to the second, [the money] was liened to the first, so that even what he gave it was not really its own.

notes.he: ההיא ערך (ההיא ערך) אחרון היינו בעל חוב מאוחר שקדם וגבה מה שגבה גבה. כלומר כולהי הוו משעבדי לראשונה אי לאו דקדמה שנייה ומה שקדמה וגבתה זכתה בו הך חדא דשיירה משעבדא לראשונה ובעידנא דיהב לראשונה חד יצא דתו לא אית ליה דאין ידו משגת יותר הילכך יצא ידי שתיהם:
notes.en: A later creditor: that last valuation is the later creditor who collected first; what he collected he collected. That is, all [five] would have been liened to the first had the second not preceded it; and what the second preceded and collected, it acquired. The one that remained was liened to the first, and at the time he gave one to the first, he fulfilled it, since he had nothing more and his means did not suffice for more. Therefore he fulfilled both of them.]

messages.text: In this case, since at the time that he gave the four sela for the second vow, his possessions were liened for the payment of his first vow, it is as though he had no possessions at all with which to pay the second vow, and he therefore fulfilled the second vow even though he paid less than the full amount of money in his possession.

Then, at the time he gave one sela for payment of the first vow, he in fact had no more than one sela, as he had given the other four sela in payment of the second vow, and therefore he fulfills his obligation by paying one sela.

notes.he: תימה דבעידנא דנדר לראשון היה לו ה' סלעים ואיך מפטר כשנתן להם אחת התנן פרק השג יד (לקמן ערכין דף יז:) היה עשיר פי' בשעת הנדר והעני כשבא לפרוע לכהן או עני כשנדר ולא נתן כלום והעשיר נותן ערך עשיר ואומר רבינו דהך דלקמן דוקא שהעריכו הכהן בעודו עשיר ולכך כשהעני שוב נותן ערך עשיר אבל אם נדר כשהוא עשיר ולא הוערך והעני נותן ערך עני ובשמעתין הכי הוא נתן ד' לשניה שהכהן העריכו תחילה על השניה וחזר והעריכו על הראשון ונתן על פיו אחד על הראשון ולכך נפטר ממנה דלא הוערך עליה בעוד שהיו בידו החמש סלעים:
notes.en: At the time that he gives to the first, he has nothing: This is puzzling, since at the time that he vowed the first, he had five sela; so how is he exempted when he gave it one? But we learned in chapter HaSeg Yad (below, Arakhin 17b): If he was wealthy, meaning at the time of the vow, and became poor [when he came to pay the priest], or he was poor [when he vowed], gave nothing, and became wealthy, he gives the valuation of a wealthy man. And our teacher says that the mishna below is specifically where the priest assessed him while he was still wealthy, and therefore when he becomes poor he still gives the valuation of a wealthy man; but if he vowed when he was wealthy and was not assessed, and became poor, he gives the valuation of a poor man. And in our discussion this is how it was: he gave four for the second, since the priest assessed him first for the second, and then assessed him again for the first, and according to [the priest’s assessment] he gave one for the first. Therefore he is exempt from it, since he was not assessed for it while the five sela were in his possession.

messages.caption: Paying a valuation of fifty with little money: the mishna’s cases, and Rav Adda bar Ahava’s five sela split between two vows.

messages.text: Continues on 8a: if instead he gave four sela for the first vow and one for the second, he has fulfilled only the second; then Rav Adda bar Ahava asks about one who vowed his valuation twice at once.
